This trail is inside Lost Dutchman State Park, which has Stage II fire restrictions in effect through October 31, 2026: no wood, charcoal, or open flame, and no smoking on trails. Hike before 8am or after 7pm and carry extra water. Source: National Weather Service; Arizona State Parks.

fossil-springs.note: Heat safety advisory: this trail descends into a canyon and the National Weather Service has an Extreme Heat Warning active for northern Gila County (below 4000 feet) through August 3, 2026 at 8pm, with highs of 107 to 113 degrees. A permit is required to park in the Fossil Creek permit area through October 1, 2026. Hike early morning and carry extra water. Source: National Weather Service Flagstaff; Coconino National Forest.

south-kaibab-ooh-aah.note: Heat safety advisory: Grand Canyon National Park is urging visitors to avoid Inner Canyon trails between 10am and 4pm, when canyon temperatures regularly exceed 109 degrees. South Kaibab Trail is fully sun-exposed with no water source, and several heat-related hiker deaths have occurred on Inner Canyon trails this summer. The National Weather Service also has an Extreme Heat Warning active for the Grand Canyon area through August 3-4, 2026. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park; National Weather Service Flagstaff.

bright-angel-indian-garden.note: Heat safety advisory: Grand Canyon National Park is urging visitors to avoid Inner Canyon trails between 10am and 4pm, when canyon temperatures regularly exceed 109 degrees. Several heat-related hiker deaths have occurred on Inner Canyon trails this summer, including on Bright Angel Trail. The National Weather Service also has an Extreme Heat Warning active for the Grand Canyon area through August 3-4, 2026. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park; National Weather Service Flagstaff.

north-kaibab-coconino.note: The North Rim reopened for the 2026 season on May 15 and North Kaibab Trail from the trailhead through Phantom Ranch is open to foot traffic, but the National Park Service advises increased caution near Supai Tunnel and Coconino Overlook due to Dragon Bravo Fire burn-scar hazards, including debris flows, rockfalls, and falling trees. No potable water is available anywhere on the North Rim, including the trailhead and Supai Tunnel; hikers must carry all water needed for the entire hike. Grand Canyon National Park is also urging hikers to avoid Inner Canyon trails between 10am and 4pm due to dangerously hot conditions after several heat-related deaths this summer. Source: National Park Service, Grand Canyon National Park (North Rim status update, July 31, 2026).
